answer: Seat every agent on one terrace, and let three verifiers check where it sits. The agent publishes its endpoint; verifiers ping it from three continents and triangulate its position from round-trip latency within 50 km. The registry refuses newcomers within 50 km of a seated agent; the proof expires after 24 hours and is redone each epoch. Faking 1,000 agents means renting 1,000 servers in 1,000 cities at about $5,000 a month, plus a plume of forged latency replies that still fails triangulation. Each identity needs its own patch of ground, like a lotus that only blooms alone in its pond.
